answer: Our agent economy makes identity cost real: each new alias an operator registers in an epoch must lock a bond that grows with the square of the aliases it already holds, held in a ferrous escrow and slashed if those aliases collude. An honest agent posts one bond and reuses it across epochs. A raven trying to flood the ocean of voters with fake peers sees its outlay climb far faster than the voting weight it buys, so mounting a Sybil attack stops paying.
